chapterTitle: The Woman, the Child and the Dragon
themeTitle: “They Overcame Him Because of the Lamb’s Blood”

scripture.text: A great sign was seen in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ σημεῖον μέγα ὤφθη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, “A great sign was seen in heaven” — σημεῖον, from the signs family: a sign that points beyond itself, as distinct from τέρας, a wonder; ὁράω, from the see family. Chapters 12–14 step back to show the spiritual war behind all of history. γυνὴ περιβεβλημένη τὸν ἥλιον, καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτῆς, “a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet” — καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς στέφανος ἀστέρων δώδεκα, “and on her head a crown of twelve stars” — στέφανος, from the crown family: a victor's wreath. Joseph dreamed of the sun, moon and eleven stars bowing to him — his father, mother and brothers, Israel. The woman is the people of God, who gave birth to the Messiah; Christians have also seen in her Mary, His mother.

scripture.text: She was with child. She cried out in pain, laboring to give birth.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα, “She was with child” — καὶ κράζει ὠδίνουσα καὶ βασανιζομένη τεκεῖν, “She cried out in pain, laboring to give birth” — ὠδίνω, the pains of childbirth; βασανίζω, torment; τίκτω, from the birth family: to bring forth, as distinct from γεννάω, to beget. Isaiah and Micah pictured Zion in labour, bringing forth the Messiah and a new people. The long suffering of Israel waiting for the Christ.

scripture.text: Another sign was seen in heaven. Behold, a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven crowns.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὤφθη ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, “Another sign was seen in heaven” — ἄλλος, from the another family: another of the same kind, a second sign alongside the first, as distinct from ἕτερος, another of a different kind; σημεῖον, from the signs family; ὁράω, from the see family. καὶ ἰδοὺ δράκων μέγας πυρρός, “Behold, a great red dragon” — δράκων, a monstrous serpent, identified in verse 9 as Satan; red, the colour of blood and murder (6:4). ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ καὶ κέρατα δέκα, “having seven heads and ten horns” — like Daniel's fourth beast: total, worldly power. καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ἑπτὰ διαδήματα, “and on his heads seven crowns” — διάδημα, from the crown family: the royal diadem of ruling authority, not the στέφανος of victory. He claims to rule; the woman has won.

scripture.text: His tail drew one third of the stars of the sky, and threw them to the earth. The dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth he might devour her child.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἡ οὐρὰ αὐτοῦ σύρει τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν γῆν, “His tail drew one third of the stars of the sky, and threw them to the earth” — γῆ, from the world family. Daniel's little horn threw down some of the host of heaven; many see here the angels who fell with Satan. καὶ ὁ δράκων ἕστηκεν ἐνώπιον τῆς γυναικὸς τῆς μελλούσης τεκεῖν, “The dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth” — τίκτω, from the birth family. ἵνα ὅταν τέκῃ τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς καταφάγῃ, “so that when she gave birth he might devour her child” — τέκνον, from the children family: Herod's slaughter of the infants of Bethlehem was one face of this ancient hatred.

scripture.text: She gave birth to a son, a male child, who is to rule all the nations with a rod of iron. Her child was caught up to God, and to his throne.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἔτεκεν υἱὸν ἄρσεν, “She gave birth to a son, a male child” — τίκτω, from the birth family. ὃς μέλλει ποιμαίνειν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ, “who is to rule all the nations with a rod of iron” — Psalm 2: this child is the Messiah. ποιμαίνω, to shepherd and rule. καὶ ἡρπάσθη τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ πρὸς τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ, “Her child was caught up to God, and to his throne” — ἁρπάζω, to snatch away; τέκνον, from the children family. The whole life of Jesus, from birth to ascension, in one sentence: the dragon failed to devour Him; the cross became the path to the throne.

scripture.text: The woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that there they may nourish her one thousand two hundred sixty days.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἔφυγεν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον, “The woman fled into the wilderness” — ἔρημος: as Israel fled from Egypt into the wilderness, and Elijah fled from Jezebel, and Mary and Joseph fled to Egypt. Now the woman is the church after Christ's ascension. ὅπου ἔχει ἐκεῖ τόπον ἡτοιμασμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, “where she has a place prepared by God” — ἵνα ἐκεῖ τρέφωσιν αὐτὴν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα, “that there they may nourish her one thousand two hundred sixty days” — ἡμέρα, from the time family: the same period as the two witnesses (11:3). The wilderness is a place of danger, but also of God's provision, like manna.

scripture.text: There was war in the sky. Michael and his angels made war on the dragon. The dragon and his angels made war.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἐγένετο πόλεμος ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, “There was war in the sky” — πόλεμος. ὁ Μιχαὴλ καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ τοῦ πολεμῆσαι μετὰ τοῦ δράκοντος, “Michael and his angels made war on the dragon” — Μιχαήλ, ‘Who is like God?’: in Daniel the great prince who protects God's people. καὶ ὁ δράκων ἐπολέμησεν καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ, “The dragon and his angels made war” — the heavenly side of the battle won on earth at the cross (v. 11).

scripture.text: They didn’t prevail, neither was a place found for them any more in heaven.
scripture.understanding: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν, “They didn’t prevail” — ἰσχύω, from the power family: to have strength, to be able; the dragon's force is not enough. οὐδὲ τόπος εὑρέθη αὐτῶν ἔτι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, “neither was a place found for them any more in heaven” — εὑρίσκω. The woman has a place prepared by God (v. 6); the dragon loses his.

scripture.text: The great dragon was thrown down, the old serpent, he who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐβλήθη ὁ δράκων ὁ μέγας, “The great dragon was thrown down” — βάλλω, passive: thrown out by God. ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος, “the old serpent” — the serpent of Eden. ὁ καλούμενος Διάβολος καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς, “he who is called the devil and Satan” — διάβολος, the slanderer (Greek); Σατανᾶς, the adversary (Hebrew). ὁ πλανῶν τὴν οἰκουμένην ὅλην, “the deceiver of the whole world” — πλανάω, present tense: he keeps on deceiving; οἰκουμένη, from the world family: the inhabited earth. ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν, “He was thrown down to the earth” — γῆ, from the world family. Five names, one enemy: dragon, serpent, devil, Satan, deceiver.

scripture.text: I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying, “Now the salvation, the power, and the Kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ has come; for the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accuses them before our God day and night.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λέγουσαν, “I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying” — Ἄρτι ἐγένετο ἡ σωτηρία καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ, “Now the salvation, the power, and the Kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ has come” — δύναμις and ἐξουσία, two members of the power family: God's inherent might and Christ's rightful authority. ἄρτι, now: through the cross and resurrection. ὅτι ἐβλήθη ὁ κατήγωρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἡμῶν, “for the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down” — κατήγωρ, the prosecutor in court. ὁ κατηγορῶν αὐτοὺς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, “who accuses them before our God day and night” — ἡμέρα, from the time family. As in Job and Zechariah, Satan's role is to accuse. His case is now thrown out of court.

scripture.text: They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn’t love their life, even to death.
scripture.understanding: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐνίκησαν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀρνίου, “They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood” — νικάω; ἀρνίον, from the lamb family. The accuser's charges are answered by the blood: their sins are paid for. καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς μαρτυρίας αὐτῶν, “and because of the word of their testimony” — λόγος, from the word family; μαρτυρία, from the witness family. καὶ οὐκ ἠγάπησαν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτῶν ἄχρι θανάτου, “They didn’t love their life, even to death” — ἀγαπάω, from the love family; ψυχή, from the life family: their natural life, as distinct from ζωή, the life of God. Three weapons: the blood of Christ, the word of witness, and a love for Him greater than love of life.

scripture.text: Therefore rejoice, heavens, and you who dwell in them. Woe to the earth and to the sea, because the devil has gone down to you, having great wrath, knowing that he has but a short time.”
scripture.understanding: διὰ τοῦτο εὐφραίνεσθε, οὐρανοὶ καὶ οἱ ἐν αὐτοῖς σκηνοῦντες, “Therefore rejoice, heavens, and you who dwell in them” — σκηνόω, to dwell as in a tent: those who belong to heaven, in contrast to ‘those who dwell on the earth’. οὐαὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν, “Woe to the earth and to the sea” — οὐαί; γῆ, from the world family. ὅτι κατέβη ὁ διάβολος πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔχων θυμὸν μέγαν, “because the devil has gone down to you, having great wrath” — θυμός, from the wrath family: hot, passionate rage, as distinct from God's settled ὀργή (6:16). εἰδὼς ὅτι ὀλίγον καιρὸν ἔχει, “knowing that he has but a short time” — οἶδα, from the know family and the see family; καιρός, from the time family: his season is short. The devil is furious because he is defeated.

scripture.text: When the dragon saw that he was thrown down to the earth, he persecuted the woman who gave birth to the male child.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ὅτε εἶδεν ὁ δράκων ὅτι ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν, “When the dragon saw that he was thrown down to the earth” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); γῆ, from the world family. ἐδίωξεν τὴν γυναῖκα ἥτις ἔτεκεν τὸν ἄρσενα, “he persecuted the woman who gave birth to the male child” — διώκω, to pursue, to persecute; τίκτω, from the birth family. Unable to reach Christ, Satan attacks His people. Jesus asked Saul, ‘why are you persecuting me?’ — to persecute the church is to persecute Christ.

scripture.text: Two wings of the great eagle were given to the woman, that she might fly into the wilderness to her place, so that she might be nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐδόθησαν τῇ γυναικὶ αἱ δύο πτέρυγες τοῦ ἀετοῦ τοῦ μεγάλου, “Two wings of the great eagle were given to the woman” — God told Israel at Sinai, ‘I bore you on eagles’ wings, and brought you to myself.’ ἵνα πέτηται εἰς τὴν ἔρημον εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς, “that she might fly into the wilderness to her place” — ὅπου τρέφεται ἐκεῖ καιρὸν καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἥμισυ καιροῦ, “so that she might be nourished for a time, and times, and half a time” — καιρός, from the time family, three times: Daniel's phrase, three and a half ‘times’, the same as the 1,260 days of verse 6. ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ ὄφεως, “from the face of the serpent.”

scripture.text: The serpent spewed water out of his mouth after the woman like a river, that he might cause her to be carried away by the stream.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ὄφις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ὀπίσω τῆς γυναικὸς ὕδωρ ὡς ποταμόν, “The serpent spewed water out of his mouth after the woman like a river” — a flood of lies and persecution from the mouth of the deceiver. ἵνα αὐτὴν ποταμοφόρητον ποιήσῃ, “that he might cause her to be carried away by the stream” — ποταμοφόρητος, swept away by a river: the psalmist prayed to be rescued from overwhelming waters.

scripture.text: The earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river which the dragon spewed out of his mouth.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐβοήθησεν ἡ γῆ τῇ γυναικί, “The earth helped the woman” — βοηθέω, to run to help; γῆ, from the world family. Creation itself takes God's side. καὶ ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ στόμα αὐτῆς καὶ κατέπιεν τὸν ποταμὸν ὃν ἔβαλεν ὁ δράκων ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, “and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river which the dragon spewed out of his mouth” — as the earth opened and swallowed Korah's rebels, and as the Red Sea opened for Israel. God's protection is resourceful.

scripture.text: The dragon grew angry with the woman, and went away to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep God’s commandments and hold Jesus’ testimony.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὠργίσθη ὁ δράκων ἐπὶ τῇ γυναικί, “The dragon grew angry with the woman” — ὀργίζω, from the wrath family: to become enraged. καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν λοιπῶν τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτῆς, “and went away to make war with the rest of her offspring” — σπέρμα, seed: God promised in Eden enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. The woman is the church as a whole, kept by God; ‘the rest of her offspring’ are individual believers, who face the battle. τῶν τηρούντων τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ, “who keep God’s commandments and hold Jesus’ testimony” — τηρέω, from the hold family; μαρτυρία, from the witness family. The marks of the church under attack: obedience and witness.

visualMeditations.title: The Woman and the Dragon
visualMeditations.image: Picture a woman in the sky, robed in sunlight, standing on the moon, crowned with twelve stars, crying out in labour. Facing her, a gigantic blood-red dragon with seven crowned heads and ten horns, its tail sweeping stars out of the sky, crouching to devour her baby the moment it is born.
visualMeditations.meaning: “The dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth he might devour her child” (v. 4). Behind the story of Israel and the birth of Jesus lies a cosmic war. The enemy has always tried to destroy God's saving purpose — and always failed.

visualMeditations.title: Caught Up to the Throne
visualMeditations.image: Picture the dragon lunging — and the child snatched up out of his reach, carried into the very throne of God. The woman runs into the desert, where a place has been prepared, and she is fed there day by day.
visualMeditations.meaning: “Her child was caught up to God, and to his throne. The woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God” (vv. 5–6). Christ is safe on the throne; His church is kept and fed in the wilderness of this world.

visualMeditations.title: The Accuser Thrown Down
visualMeditations.image: Picture a courtroom in heaven. Day and night the prosecutor stands before the Judge, reading out the sins of God's people. Then the case is thrown out: the accuser is hurled out of court and out of heaven, and a voice cries, ‘Now salvation has come!’ On earth, believers stand with a cross behind them and testimony on their lips.
visualMeditations.meaning: “The accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accuses them before our God day and night. They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn’t love their life, even to death” (vv. 10–11).

visualMeditations.title: Eagle's Wings and a Swallowed Flood
visualMeditations.image: Picture the woman running from the furious dragon. Suddenly great eagle's wings are given to her, and she flies into the desert. The serpent spews a torrent after her — and the ground cracks open and drinks the river down.
visualMeditations.meaning: “Two wings of the great eagle were given to the woman, that she might fly into the wilderness to her place” (v. 14). “The earth helped the woman” (v. 16). God has more ways of protecting His people than the enemy has of attacking them.

structure.label: The Woman and the Dragon (v. 1-6)
structure.body: A great sign appears in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, the moon under her feet, crowned with twelve stars, in labour; another sign: a great red dragon with seven heads, ten horns and seven diadems, who sweeps down a third of the stars and waits to devour her child; she bears a son who will rule the nations, and he is caught up to God's throne; the woman flees into the wilderness to a place prepared by God for 1,260 days.

structure.label: War in Heaven (v. 7-12)
structure.body: Michael and his angels fight the dragon and his angels, who are defeated and thrown down to the earth; the dragon is identified as the ancient serpent, the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; a voice in heaven proclaims that salvation and God's kingdom have come, because the accuser is thrown down; believers have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony; heaven rejoices, but woe to earth and sea, for the devil has come down in great fury, knowing his time is short.

structure.label: The Dragon Pursues the Woman (v. 13-17)
structure.body: The dragon persecutes the woman, but she is given eagle's wings to fly to her place in the wilderness for a time, times and half a time; the serpent pours a river after her, but the earth swallows it; enraged, the dragon goes off to make war on the rest of her offspring, who keep God's commandments and hold to the testimony of Jesus.

sections.heading: The Great Conflict Behind History
paragraphs: Chapter 11 brought us to the seventh trumpet and the coming of the kingdom. Chapter 12 goes back to show the deep cause of all the conflict in the book: a war between God and the dragon, fought out in the story of Christ and His people. Chapters 12–14 introduce the enemy and his allies — the dragon (ch. 12), the beast from the sea and the beast from the land (ch. 13) — and God's answer (ch. 14).

John sees two ‘signs’. The first is “a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars” (v. 1). In Joseph's dream the sun, moon and stars were his family — Israel. The woman is the people of God, from whom the Messiah came. Christians have often seen Mary in her too, as the individual through whom that people brought forth the Christ; and from verse 6 onward she is clearly the church, God's people after Christ's ascension. The strongest reading holds these together: she is the one people of God, Old and New.

The second sign is “a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven crowns” (v. 3). He is named in verse 9: “the old serpent, he who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world.” From Eden onward, he has tried to destroy the woman's offspring, as God foretold to the serpent: there would be enmity between his seed and hers.

sections.heading: The Birth and Ascension of the Child
paragraphs: The dragon stands before the woman, ready to devour her child the moment He is born (v. 4). Behind Pharaoh's slaughter of Hebrew boys, behind Herod's massacre at Bethlehem, behind every attempt to destroy the line of the Messiah, stands the dragon. An angel warned Joseph: “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt... for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him” (Matthew 2:13).

“She gave birth to a son, a male child, who is to rule all the nations with a rod of iron. Her child was caught up to God, and to his throne” (v. 5). In one sentence John moves from Christ's birth to His ascension. The dragon failed. Even when he seemed to win at the cross, Christ rose and was caught up to the throne. Paul says that Christ, “having stripped the principalities and the powers, he made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in it” (Colossians 2:15).

Then “The woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that there they may nourish her one thousand two hundred sixty days” (v. 6). The 1,260 days are the same period as the witness of the two prophets (11:3) — the time of the church between Christ's ascension and return. The wilderness is a place of danger and testing, as it was for Israel after the Exodus. But it is also a place where God feeds His people, as He fed Israel with manna.

sections.heading: The Accuser Thrown Down
paragraphs: “There was war in the sky” (v. 7). Michael and his angels fight the dragon and his angels, and the dragon loses: “The great dragon was thrown down... He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him” (v. 9). This is not simply a description of an ancient fall of Satan before creation. The song that follows makes clear when it happens: “Now the salvation, the power, and the Kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ has come” (v. 10). Satan's defeat in heaven is the result of Christ's victory on earth. Jesus said, as the cross approached, “Now is the judgment of this world. Now the prince of this world will be cast out” (John 12:31).

Satan is called “the accuser of our brothers... who accuses them before our God day and night” (v. 10). In Zechariah's vision, Satan stood at Joshua the high priest's right hand to accuse him, and God answered, “Yahweh rebuke you, Satan!” (Zechariah 3:2). Satan's accusations are often true — we have sinned. But Christ's death has answered them. Paul asks, “Who could bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? It is God who justifies” (Romans 8:33).

And so the saints conquer: “They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn’t love their life, even to death” (v. 11). The blood of the Lamb answers every accusation. The word of testimony declares Christ's victory. And a love for Christ greater than love for life makes them unafraid of the worst the dragon can do.

sections.heading: The Dragon's Last Rage
paragraphs: Heaven rejoices, but earth is warned: “Woe to the earth and to the sea, because the devil has gone down to you, having great wrath, knowing that he has but a short time” (v. 12). The devil's fury on earth is not a sign of his strength but of his defeat. He knows his time is short. This explains much of the suffering of the church: a beaten enemy lashing out.

He persecutes the woman (v. 13), but God gives her “Two wings of the great eagle” (v. 14), recalling God's words at Sinai that He carried Israel on eagles' wings. He spews a flood after her, but “The earth helped the woman” (v. 16). God's people as a whole cannot be destroyed.

So the dragon turns on individual believers: he “went away to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep God’s commandments and hold Jesus’ testimony” (v. 17). The church as a body is safe; its members will be attacked. Their marks are obedience to God and faithful witness to Jesus. Peter wrote, “Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour. Withstand him steadfast in your faith” (1 Peter 5:8–9). The next chapter shows the instruments the dragon will use.

ntConnection.heading: The Defeat of the Devil
paragraphs: The New Testament everywhere teaches that Christ's death and resurrection defeated Satan. Jesus “partook of the same, that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death, that is, the devil” (Hebrews 2:14). He said, “I saw Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven” (Luke 10:18) and “Now the prince of this world will be cast out” (John 12:31).

Paul answers the accuser: “Who is he who condemns? It is Christ who died, yes rather, who was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us” (Romans 8:34). And he promises, “And the God of peace will quickly crush Satan under your feet” (Romans 16:20) — the final fulfilment of God's word to the serpent in Eden.
The birth of the child echoes Paul's summary of the incarnation: “But when the fullness of the time came, God sent out his Son, born to a woman, born under the law” (Galatians 4:4).

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “a fabulous kind of serpent (perhaps as supposed to fascinate).” δράκων, a great serpent or sea-monster, appears thirteen times in Revelation and nowhere else in the New Testament. The Old Testament spoke of Leviathan and Rahab, sea monsters God crushed — pictures of chaos and of Egypt. Revelation identifies the dragon plainly: ‘the old serpent, he who is called the devil and Satan’ (v. 9). He is red with blood, crowned with stolen authority, and doomed.

Strong's: “against one in the assembly, i.e. a complainant at law; specially, Satan.” κατήγωρ is the prosecutor who brings charges in court — the meaning of the Hebrew ‘Satan’. In Job and Zechariah he stands before God accusing the righteous. His accusations against believers are thrown out because the Lamb's blood has paid every debt. When guilt and condemnation press on you, remember: the accuser has been thrown down.

Strong's: “to seize (in various applications).” ἁρπάζω means to snatch, to seize suddenly and with force. It is used of the Spirit catching Philip away, of Paul being caught up to the third heaven, and of believers being ‘caught up’ to meet the Lord in the air (1 Thessalonians 4:17). Here the Child is snatched up to God's throne out of the dragon's reach: Christ's ascension is His decisive escape and enthronement.

Strong's: “to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively).” ὠδίνω is the agony of childbirth. Paul uses it of his longing for converts — ‘my little children, of whom I am again in travail until Christ is formed in you’ (Galatians 4:19) — and of creation groaning in labour (Romans 8:22). Jesus called the troubles before the end ‘birth pains’ (Matthew 24:8). The woman's pain is the long suffering of God's people before the Messiah came; but labour pains end in new life.

Strong's: “an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally.” σημεῖον, from the signs family, is something that points beyond itself — as distinct from τέρας, a wonder that amazes, and δύναμις, a mighty work. John's Gospel calls Jesus' miracles ‘signs’. Here the woman and the dragon are ‘signs’: they are not literal creatures in the sky but pictures that reveal what is happening in history. The false prophet will also do ‘great signs’ (13:13) — counterfeits that point the wrong way.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit shows you the war behind your struggles — and the victory already won.

items.title: The Accuser Has Lost His Case
items.body: Satan accuses believers “before our God day and night” (v. 10), but he has been thrown down. The Spirit wants you to stop listening to the voice of condemnation. When the accuser reminds you of your sins, answer with the blood of the Lamb: it has paid for them all.

items.title: Overcome the Way the Saints Do
items.body: “They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn’t love their life, even to death” (v. 11). The Spirit gives you the same weapons: trust in Christ's blood, speak your testimony, and love Jesus more than your own comfort or life.

items.title: God Has Prepared a Place for You
items.body: The woman has “a place prepared by God” in the wilderness, where she is fed (v. 6). If you are in a wilderness season, the Spirit wants you to know that God has prepared it, and He will nourish you there. You will not be swept away.

audit.title: The Accusation Check
audit.body: What accusations does the enemy most often whisper to you about your past or your worth? How does the blood of the Lamb answer them (vv. 10–11)?

audit.title: The Testimony Check
audit.body: When did you last tell someone what Jesus has done for you (v. 11)?

audit.title: The Love-of-Life Check
audit.body: What would you be unwilling to lose for Jesus — comfort, reputation, safety, relationships (v. 11)?

practices.title: Answer the Accuser
practices.body: Write down three accusations you often hear in your mind. Beside each, write a Bible verse about Christ's forgiveness (for example, Romans 8:1, 1 John 1:9, Revelation 12:11). Each time the accusation comes this week, read the verse aloud.

practices.title: Write Your Testimony
practices.body: Write a one-page account of how Jesus has saved and changed you. Practise telling it in three minutes. Pray for an opportunity to share it this week (v. 11).

prayerReflection: “Lord Jesus, You are the Child the dragon could not devour, caught up to the throne of God, who will rule the nations. Thank You that You have defeated the ancient serpent, the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. Thank You that the accuser of my brothers and sisters has been thrown down. When he accuses me, I plead Your blood. Now salvation and power and the kingdom of our God and the authority of His Christ have come! Give me grace to overcome as Your saints do: by Your blood, by the word of my testimony, and by loving You more than my own life. Thank You for the place You have prepared for Your people in the wilderness, and for feeding us there. Carry us on eagle's wings. When the enemy pours out a flood of lies or persecution, open the earth to swallow it. Help me keep God's commandments and hold fast the testimony of Jesus. Amen.”

storyConnections.title: The Serpent in the Garden
storyConnections.summary: In Eden the serpent deceived Eve, and through her Adam, and sin and death entered the world. But God said to the serpent, ‘I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.’ Revelation 12 calls the dragon ‘the old serpent’ and shows the long war between his offspring and the woman's, until the Child is caught up to the throne and the serpent is thrown down. The promise of Eden is kept.

storyConnections.title: Herod and the Infants of Bethlehem
storyConnections.summary: When wise men came asking for the newborn King of the Jews, Herod was troubled. He tried to trick them into revealing the child's location, and when they did not return, he killed all the boys in Bethlehem two years old and under. But an angel had warned Joseph: “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt” (Matthew 2:13). Herod's rage was one face of the dragon standing before the woman to devour her child — and God's protection was stronger.

storyConnections.title: Joshua the High Priest Accused
storyConnections.summary: Zechariah saw “Joshua the high priest standing before Yahweh’s angel, and Satan standing at his right hand to be his adversary” (Zechariah 3:1). Joshua was dressed in filthy clothes. But the LORD rebuked Satan, and the angel ordered the filthy garments removed and clean robes put on him, saying, ‘I have caused your iniquity to pass from you.’ This is what the Lamb's blood does for every believer: the accuser is silenced, and the filthy garments are replaced with white.
